'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Corruption in Ukraine]]
***A [[Government of Ukraine|government]] investigation uncovers [[corruption]] at [[Military recruitment|recruitment centres]] in 11 regions with 112 criminal proceedings opened. Bribes averaged around [[US$]]6,000 for a medical certificate granting an exemption from military service. [https://www.ft.com/content/b6851dac-0c9e-4e8e-a502-39b029827a07 (''Financial Times'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/aug/11/zelenskiy-sacks-all-military-recruitment-heads-over-frontline-bribes-scandal-ukraine (''The Guardian'')]
***Investigative news website [[Dzerkalo Tyzhnia]] reveals documents showing the [[Ministry of Defence (Ukraine)|Ministry of Defence]] overpaid for summer camouflage kits bought as winter coats for troops. The documents are suspected to be related to a investigation launched in June by Ukraine’s [[Security Service of Ukraine|security services]] into Former Deputy Defense Minister [[Vyacheslav Shapovalov]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/aug/11/zelenskiy-sacks-all-military-recruitment-heads-over-frontline-bribes-scandal-ukraine (''The Guardian'')]
***A ''[[New York Times]]'' investigation reveals that a company tied to [[Serhiy Pashynskyi]], who was previously under investigation for corruption, has become the biggest private arms supplier to the [[Ministry of Defence (Ukraine)|Ministry of Defence]]. [https://www.businessinsider.com/serhiy-pashinsky-ukraine-relies-on-arms-dealer-accused-of-corruption-2023-8 (Insider)]
**[[Crimea attacks (2022–present)|Crimea attacks]]
***The [[Ministry of Defense (Russia)|Russian Ministry of Defense]] says that it shot down twenty [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drones]] over [[Crimea]]. [https://nos.nl/liveblog/2485729-rusland-20-drones-neergehaald-boven-krim-training-oekraiense-piloten-in-vs-duurt-langer (NOS)] 
***[[Head of the Republic of Crimea]] [[Sergey Aksyonov]] says that three Ukrainian missiles were shot down over the [[Crimean Bridge|Kerch bridge]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/russia-ukraine-war-new-08-12-23/index.html (CNN International)]
**[[Minister of Defence (Russia)|Russian Defence Minister]] [[Sergei Shoigu]] inspects the [[Northern Fleet]] and visits a [[Rosatom]] [[Novaya Zemlya#Nuclear testing|nuclear weapons test site]] in [[Novaya Zemlya]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/russias-shoigu-inspects-northern-fleet-warships-sent-arctic-2023-08-12/ (Reuters)] [https://www.hindustantimes.com/videos/world-news/putin-sends-defence-min-shoigu-to-inspect-russian-nuclear-site-in-the-arctic-as-war-rages-watch-101691846023169-amp.html (''Hindustan Times'')] [https://thebarentsobserver.com/en/security/2023/08/after-blaming-west-waging-proxy-war-russia-shoigu-went-arctic-nuclear-test-site (''The Barents Observer'')]
**One person is killed and 12 others are injured in a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[Guided bomb|guided]] [[aerial bomb]] strike on [[Orikhiv]], [[Zaporizhzhia Oblast]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/russia-ukraine-war-new-08-12-23/h_f14405bf53cf3535887ad7af1b3fefd5 (CNN International)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Hawaii wildfires]]
**The death toll from the [[wildfire]]s in [[Maui]], [[Hawaii]], [[United States]], increases to 89, making it the deadliest wildfire in the [[History of Hawaii|state's history]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/climate-change/news/maui-fires-hawaii-wildfires-cause-b2391921.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[2023 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[2023 Pacific hurricane season#Hurricane Dora|Hurricane Dora]], which partially caused the wildfires in Hawaii, becomes a [[2023 Pacific typhoon season#Typhoon Dora|Pacific typhoon]]. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/marshallshepherd/2023/08/12/hurricane-dora-is-now-a-typhoon-but-did-it-make-the-maui-fires-worse/amp/ (Forbes)] [https://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/2023/08/12/hurricane-dora-makes-history-without-making-landfall/?outputType=amp (Hawaii News Now)]
*[[English Channel migrant crossings (2018–present)|English Channel migrant crossings]]
**Six people are killed and fifty others are rescued when a boat carrying migrants [[capsize]]s in the [[English Channel]] off the coast of [[Calais]], [[France]]. [https://apnews.com/article/migrants-small-boats-english-channel-crossing-drowned-4e3c6583d26e111fe1e1a62c8dffe7d3 (AP)]
*[[Fukushima nuclear disaster]]
**[[Koreans|South Korean]]s gather in central [[Seoul]] to protest against [[Japan]]'s plan to release treated radioactive water from the [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant|Fukushima nuclear power plant]] into the ocean. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-korean-activists-protest-against-fukushima-water-discharge-2023-08-12/ (Reuters)]
*Four people are killed and one other injured following a house explosion in [[Allegheny County, Pennsylvania|Allegheny]], [[Pennsylvania]], United States, that destroyed three structures and damaged at least a dozen others. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/08/14/world/4-people-dead-1-missing-after-explosion-destroys-3-structures-in-western-pennsylvania/1905305 (AP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*A [[Sukhoi Su-30]] crashes during a training mission in [[Kaliningrad Oblast]], [[Russia]], killing both pilots. [https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-fighter-jet-crash-kaliningrad/32545374.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Ecuadorian general election]]
**[[Ecuador]] transfers head of the [[Los Choneros]] criminal group, Jose Adolfo Macias, from Prison 8 in [[Guayaquil]] to La Roca maximum security prison. He is accused of threatening [[President of Ecuador|presidential]] candidate [[Fernando Villavicencio]] before his [[Assassination of Fernando Villavicencio|assassination]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/08/13/world/gang-boss-who-threatened-slain-ecuador-candidate-transferred-to-max-security/1905185 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*Italian police recover 266 [[antique]]s from the [[Ancient Greece|Greek]], [[Ancient Rome|Roman]] and [[Etruscan civilization|Etruscan]] periods, worth tens of millions of [[Euro]]s, from the [[United States]]. [https://nos.nl/artikel/2486370-italie-haalt-archeologische-vondsten-terug-uit-vs-ter-waarde-van-miljoenen (NOS)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Ecuadorian general election]]
**[[Andrea González Náder]], the [[running mate]] of [[Assassination of Fernando Villavicencio|assassinated]] [[President of Ecuador|presidential]] candidate [[Fernando Villavicencio]], is nominated by the [[Movimiento Construye]] party to run for president. [https://www.news18.com/world/running-mate-of-slain-ecuadoran-candidate-to-run-for-president-8534408.html (AFP via CNN-News18)]
*[[2023 Malaysian state elections]]
**Malaysians in [[Selangor]], [[Kelantan]], [[Terengganu]], [[Negeri Sembilan]], [[Kedah]] and [[Penang]] vote for their [[State legislative assemblies of Malaysia|state assembly]] members, following the dissolution of the assemblies. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/08/13/world/asia-oceania/malaysia-holds-polls-seen-as-test-for-anwar/1905163 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[Senate of Pakistan|Senator]] [[Anwar ul Haq Kakar]] is appointed as the new [[caretaker prime minister of Pakistan]]. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/asia/pakistan-senator-anwar-ul-haq-kakar-becomes-caretaker-pm20230812161442/ (ANI News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 Arab Club Champions Cup]]
**In [[association football]], [[Football in Saudi Arabia|Saudi Arabian]] club [[Al Nassr FC]] wins their first [[Arab Club Champions Cup]] in a 2–1 victory. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2354031/saudi-football (''Arab News'')]
